title: Adding and Subtracting Numbers up to 1,000,000
seo_title: Grade 4 Addition and Subtraction Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Add numbers with sums up to 1 000 000 and subtract numbers where both numbers are less than 1 000 000, with and without regrouping.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 addition and subtraction worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: add and subtract numbers up to 1,000,000 with regrouping, across zeros and in word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the ones; work from right to left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Line up the digits by place value, starting from the ones.
  • Add or subtract one column at a time, from right to left.
  • Adding: if a column is 10 or more, regroup (carry) 1 to the next column.
  • Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, regroup (borrow) from the next column. Check by adding the answer and the number you subtracted.

Examples

Example

254,368 + 137,945

Add from the ones, regrouping 5 times

Answer: 392,313

Example

500,000 − 128,457

Regroup across the zeros

Answer: 371,543

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to regroupWrite the carried 1 above the next column.
Subtracting the smaller digit from the biggerRegroup when the top digit is smaller.
Lining up from the leftLine up the ones.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 4 ask about addition and subtraction?
faq.a: Add numbers with sums up to 1 000 000 and subtract numbers where both numbers are less than 1 000 000, with and without regrouping.

faq.q: How do I check a subtraction?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number you subtracted. You should get the first number.
Trading 10 of one place for 1 of the next place.
Yes. An estimate shows if your answer is reasonable.

items.q: A car park has 1,200 spaces. At 9 am, 785 cars are parked. By lunchtime, 296 more cars arrive. How many spaces are empty now?
A factory made 4,750 packets of cookies. It sent 1,836 packets to one shop and 2,479 packets to another shop. How many packets are left?
A concert sold 3,475 tickets online and 1,868 tickets at the door. A second concert sold 4,926 tickets. How many more tickets did the first concert sell?
items.e: Step 1, tickets for the first concert: 3,475 + 1,868 = 5,343. Step 2, find the difference: 5,343 − 4,926 = 417.

items.q: Emmanuel walked 4,568 steps on Saturday and 3,895 steps on Sunday. Rose walked 9,000 steps over the weekend. How many more steps did Rose walk than Emmanuel?
items.e: Step 1, Emmanuel’s steps: 4,568 + 3,895 = 8,463. Step 2, find the difference: 9,000 − 8,463 = 537.

items.q: A library had 4,326 books. It lent out 1,258 books, then it bought 375 new books. How many books are in the library now?
items.e: Step 1, after lending: 4,326 − 1,258 = 3,068. Step 2, after buying: 3,068 + 375 = 3,443.

items.q: A garden center had 2,405 plants. It sold 1,368 plants, then a lorry delivered 850 more. How many plants does it have now?
items.e: Step 1, after selling: 2,405 − 1,368 = 1,037. Step 2, after the delivery: 1,037 + 850 = 1,887.

items.e: Step 1, kilometers driven: 1,348 km + 1,275 km = 2,623 km. Step 2, kilometers left: 4,000 km − 2,623 km = 1,377 km. Check: 1,377 km + 2,623 km = 4,000 km.

items.q: Hazel’s school collected 1,285 books in the first week of a book drive and 968 books in the second week. It gave 1,500 books to a charity shop. How many books are left?
items.e: Step 1, books collected: 1,285 + 968 = 2,253. Step 2, find the difference: 2,253 − 1,500 = 753.
